questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing a leather jacket while riding?

options.text: It makes you look cool.
It is too warm to wear in hot weather.
It protects you if you crash.
You should not wear one while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, ideally leather, when riding. Leather jackets help protect you in a crash. They also help prevent dehydration in hot weather. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool even in heat.

questions.question: What is an easy way to make your motorcycle easier for others to see?

options.text: Attach a large flag to the motorcycle frame.
Keep your headlight turned on.
Wave at other drivers.
Ride on the road shoulder whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: Make yourself easier to see by wearing bright, reflective clothing. Keep your headlight on at all times. Use your turn signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: What type of helmet gives the most protection?

options.text: A helmet that fits loosely.
A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
A helmet that survived a previous crash.
A helmet that provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: Why should you keep a safe distance behind other vehicles?

options.text: To give you time and space to spot and react to dangers.
So you can tailgate safely.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time and space to spot and react to dangers.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also gives you a better view of hazards on the road, such as potholes.

questions.question: What happens if you take a turn too fast on a motorcycle?

options.text: It is acceptable if you stay under the speed limit.
It is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
It is acceptable if no other vehicles are nearby.
You may end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. If you cannot hold the turn, you may end up in another lane or off the road. Always be careful when turning.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is properly fastened.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is properly fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is properly fastened is the single most important thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: What should you expect when passing a row of parked cars?

options.text: Open parking spaces.
A car may suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other drivers will see you and stay out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car may suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for a car to suddenly pull out into traffic. Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This creates more space between you and any hazards.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use that lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to a vehicle in another lane is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver will not see you. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What is the proper body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent at the handle grips.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the handle grips.
Lean over the bike so your arms support your body weight.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent at the handle grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handle grips. This lets you easily and comfortably reach and operate the controls.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend who has been drinking wants to ride their motorcycle?

options.text: Let them ride.
Encourage them to use less-crowded roads.
Push their bike over.
Get other friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Do whatever you can to stop them. Get a group of friends to help prevent them from riding.

questions.question: What is allowed in a no passing zone?

options.text: A motorcycle can still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle can pass if it finishes before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle can pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: No passing zones mean no vehicle can pass. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Sturdy boots
Tennis shoes
Shoes with loose laces
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles provide the best protection. Boots with laces tied tight are best. If you wear shoes with long laces, tie them up before riding.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect a motorcycle?

options.text: It usually makes no difference in handling.
It is usually safe for new riders.
It can change how the motorcycle handles.
It helps riders get used to different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight, which changes how the motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping a group of riders small?

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
A small group can ignore traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always be trying to catch up.
It is hard to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: Small groups have several advantages. Other vehicles can pass them safely. They are less likely to get separated by traffic or red lights. Slower riders do not need to rush to catch up.

questions.question: What material offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Leather
Wool
Polyester
Silk

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather provides the most protection for motorcycle riders. Wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely when riding.

questions.question: On what surface does a motorcycle have the best traction?

options.text: Dry pavement
Gravel
Snow
Leaves

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces are dangerous for motorcycles. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates can reduce traction more than dry pavement.

questions.question: What should you know about clothing when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: It should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
It should not fully cover your arms or legs.
You should not wear a jacket in warm weather.
It can protect you in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can protect you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing protects you if you crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap, but loose enough to move freely.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Once a season.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent dangerous problems. Small technical issues are more serious on a motorcycle than a car.

questions.question: What does long-term exposure to wind noise do?

options.text: It is recommended.
It can cause hearing loss.
It is not harmful.
It is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Use proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: By looking at the tire.
Use a tire gauge.
By squeezing the tire.
By comparing it to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. An under-inflated tire can look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?

options.text: A gravel road
Dry pavement
Mud
Lane markings

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal road covers are all more dangerous for motorcycles than dry pavement.

questions.question: What can you do to make sure other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Use your headlight while riding.
Swerve within your lane to get attention.
Raise your arms.
Avoid using your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight while riding.
questions.explanation: Use your headlight to be seen at intersections. Ride in a lane position that lets you see oncoming traffic clearly. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can take action to avoid danger.

questions.question: Which action lowers your risk of a crash?

options.text: Signal your moves to other drivers.
Do not look ahead while riding.
Wear dark clothes.
Ride in spots that are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your moves to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Signal your turns and stops. Position your motorcycle where others can see it. Keep space around your bike and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles.
It gets the attention of other drivers.
Mirrors are not useful.
They should make eye contact with nearby drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes to spot any vehicles or hazards.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Time.
Drinking coffee.
Exercising.
Taking a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Time.
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to sobering up.
